cards.f: Properties of an image in a plane mirror
cards.b: Same size, same distance behind the mirror as the object is in front, upright, laterally inverted, virtual.
Rays only appear to come from it; no light actually reaches it, so it cannot be formed on a screen.
Change in direction of a light ray as it passes from one medium to another (because its speed changes).

cards.f: Light enters glass from air: which way does it bend?
cards.b: Towards the normal (it slows down). Leaving glass it bends away from the normal.
n = sin i ÷ sin r (i in air); also n = speed in air ÷ speed in material. No unit.
The angle of incidence (inside the denser material) at which the angle of refraction is 90°.
Light travels from a denser medium (glass/water) towards air AND the angle of incidence is greater than the critical angle.

cards.f: Uses of total internal reflection in optical fibres
cards.b: Telecommunications (phone, cable TV, broadband) and endoscopes.

cards.f: Principal focus of a converging lens
cards.b: The point on the principal axis where rays parallel to the axis meet after refraction.

cards.f: Image when object is beyond 2F of a converging lens
cards.b: Real, inverted, diminished, between F and 2F (camera).

cards.f: Image when object is closer than F
cards.b: Virtual, upright, enlarged, same side as the object: a magnifying glass.

cards.f: EM spectrum in order of increasing frequency
cards.b: Radio, microwaves, infrared, visible, ultraviolet, X-rays, gamma rays.

short.q: A ray enters glass with angle of incidence 45° and angle of refraction 28°. Calculate the refractive index.
Explain how light is transmitted along an optical fibre.
short.model: Light enters at one end and hits the fibre wall at an angle greater than the critical angle, so it undergoes total internal reflection again and again along the fibre.
points: angle of incidence greater than critical angle

short.q: An object is placed 3.0 cm from a converging lens of focal length 5.0 cm. Describe the image.
short.model: The object is inside F, so the image is virtual, upright and enlarged, on the same side as the object.

short.q: State two uses and one harmful effect of ultraviolet radiation.
short.model: Uses: detecting fake bank notes (and sterilising / security marking). Harmful: damage to surface cells and eyes, leading to skin cancer and eye conditions.
points: second correct use or second effect

short.q: State what happens to a ray travelling along the normal into a glass block. Explain.
short.model: It passes straight through without changing direction, though its speed decreases, because the change of direction only occurs when the ray meets the boundary at an angle.
